name: Vransko Bridge
zag_role: Bridge weigh-in-motion measurement and direct measurement of dynamic amplification
description: One of the earliest long SiWIM deployments. Strain was recorded continuously for 58 days, from 25 September to 21 November 2006, capturing 147,524 vehicles including roughly 74,000 five-axle articulated trucks. Total and static bending moments at mid-span were separated to measure the dynamic amplification directly from traffic rather than inferring it from a code factor. The work was done with University College Dublin.
history: The bridge near Vransko carries the A1 motorway at Brode and has two independent superstructures, one for each travel direction. Each is a simply supported beam and slab structure with a span of 24.8 m between supports, a total length of 26 m, a width of 12 m and no skew. It has been used as a bridge weigh in motion test site with a SiWIM system in the nothing on the road configuration, using ten strain sensors, two per beam, with additional upstream and downstream gauges for axle detection. In the study by O'Brien, González, Dowling and Žnidarič the system ran for 58 days from 25 September to 21 November 2006 and recorded 147,524 vehicles, of which about 74,000 were five axle articulated trucks. The work was part of the European ARCHES project and used the measurements to extract bridge dynamic amplification directly from traffic rather than from controlled runs. The paper states that exact static weights were not available, so no weighing accuracy figure is reported for this deployment.
facts: ten strain sensors, two per beam, plus axle detection
A1 motorway at Brode near Vransko
two independent superstructures, one per travel direction, each with five precast prestressed I girders 1.4 m high and a 0.24 m deck slab
3,300 trucks per day in one direction, as used in the ARCHES simulations

source_differences: Paper reports two first natural frequencies (4.33 Hz simulated, 5.32 Hz measured first longitudinal mode), not in record, just a caveat if used.

Record history says 'additional upstream and downstream gauges for axle detection', paper says one upstream and one downstream gauge per instrumented lane in a NOR system (no axle detectors on the pavement). Wording 'axle detection' is an interpretation.

Traffic layout: González et al. write "a two-lane simply supported structure with traffic in opposite directions", while the IM-SAFE case study describes two independent superstructures, one for each travel direction, and OpenStreetMap maps two one way decks.
Span: 25 m in the IM-SAFE case study against 24.8 m between supports and 26 m in total in O'Brien et al.
open_question: Which of the two decks carried the SiWIM system. Year of construction (González et al. call it a 10 year old bridge at the time of the 2006 measurements).

model_basis.assumed: The bearing span of 24.8 m is in the sources, but the position of the bearings along the deck is not, so no bearing axes are drawn. Girders, slab thickness and abutments are not drawn.
